content:
Equality Culture Club: Make Equality Reality Bookstore























































For the second time this year, Equality Now hosted a bookstore at the 

Make Equality Reality

 Gala

, an arts-based celebration that brings together visionary leaders, powerful performances, and global changemakers committed to advancing gender equality, to highlight some of our favourite feminist titles. The books – both fiction and non-fiction and for readers of various ages – remind us of the urgency of our work and fill us with hope that a better world is possible. From us to you, enjoy the following recommendations straight from the Equality Now library.




























A Hymn to Life

 by Gisèle Pelicot




In 

A Hymn to Life

, Gisèle Pelicot tells her story for the first time, tracing a life built over five decades, the hidden abuse of her marriage’s final decade, and the long path to healing. Part memoir, part act of defiance, it is a moving portrait of survival and courage from a woman who broke her silence, reclaimed her voice, and forced a reckoning.




This year, Equality Now honoured Gisèle with the Equality Now Trailblazer Award, which honours individuals whose actions help transform the systems, institutions, and culture that shape the lives of women and girls.

The 2026 Equality Now “Make Equality Reality” Gala celebrates courage and those who choose it, honouring Virginia Roberts Giuffre, Gisèle Pelicot and Caroline Darian
















6 min read



















Press Releases




United States


























































New York, 22 October 2026 – 

Last night in New York City, global leaders, activists, and artists gathered in a celebration of courage and the power of legal reform at Equality Now’s 

2026 Make Equality Reality Gala

, held at Cipriani 25 Broadway.




The 15th annual event focused on choosing courage in a world where women’s and girls’ rights are being undermined, bringing together changemakers who use their voices, platforms and influence to stand side by side for equality, dignity and justice.




To a standing ovation, Gisèle Pelicot and her daughter Caroline Darian were presented with the Equality Now Trailblazer Award for their ongoing advocacy that has brought much-needed attention and action to the global reality of drug-facilitated sexual assault and consent.

The Data Behind the Action: Exploring the SADC Dashboard that tracks progress on ending child marriage in Southern Africa
















9 min read



















News and Insights




End child marriage




Africa


























































Photo Credit: Cozar Photography




Every girl deserves the opportunity to learn, grow, and shape her own future. Across Southern Africa, governments, parliamentarians, civil society, and local communities are working together to strengthen laws, policies, and actions to end child marriage.




A decade after the adoption of the SADC Model Law on eradicating child marriage and protecting children already in marriage, the 

Southern African Development Community Parliamentary Forum 

 (SADC PF) and the Technical Working Group on the Implementation of the SADC Model Law on Child Marriage launch a Dashboard on core indicators tracking progress on ending child marriage and protecting girls who are already married. The Dashboard shows where action is happening, highlights what works, and points out where more effort is needed. By bringing key information together in one place, it helps advocates, policymakers, and communities monitor progress and hold everyone accountable.

title: A baby died following FGM in The Gambia. Why did the case end in acquittal?
content:
16th October 2026










A baby died following FGM in The Gambia. Why did the case end in acquittal?
















By Santana Simiyu
















14 min read



















News and Insights




End harmful practices




Africa


























































Nairobi, Kenya, September 30, 2026: 

In May 2026, The Gambia’s High Court acquitted three women prosecuted in connection with the death of an infant following female genital mutilation (FGM). The Court found that the child had died from injuries sustained during FGM, but in her ruling, Justice Janneh upheld a “no case to answer” submission by the defence on the grounds that the prosecution had failed to produce legally admissible evidence establishing the criminal responsibility of the accused. 




The case did not turn on whether FGM had taken place or caused the child’s death, but on whether investigators and prosecutors had gathered and presented sufficient admissible evidence to prove who was responsible. The judgment raises an important question for The Gambia: what does it take to turn laws prohibiting FGM into effective accountability?

sexual violence case involving a Cornell University student

Child marriage laws in Africa need more funding to protect girls
















12 min read



















News and Insights




End child marriage




Africa


























































Photo credit: Chris ImageWorld




With global funding to end child marriage falling yearly since 2019, African governments must take action to strengthen budgeting and implementation of child marriage laws.  




By 

Sally Ncube,

 Equality Now, and 

Fatou Gueye Ndir,

 Senior Regional Engagement and Advocacy Officer, Girls Not Brides




Although numerous African governments have strengthened laws against child marriage, legal protections remain widely underfunded and ineffectively enforced. Many countries have no clearly outlined, dedicated national budget line for ending child marriage. Instead, allocated money is incorporated into broader gender or social protection budgets, where funds are often difficult or impossible for auditors to trace or civil society to access. 




Funding to end child marriage is falling

International Funding to End Child Marriage: Reviewing a Decade of Investment

Girls Not Brides

Girls First Fund

Publish What You Fund
